query: how to choose a geo agency

seo.title: How to Choose a GEO Agency: A 10-Point Checklist
seo.meta_description: A practical checklist to choose a GEO agency: what to ask, what proof to expect, red flags to avoid, and how to compare proposals side by side.

h1: How to Choose a GEO Agency: A 10-Point Checklist
answer: To choose a GEO agency, ask each one to show what AI engines say about your brand today, explain exactly which pages and signals they would change first, and describe how they measure citations, AI-referred traffic and leads. Prefer agencies that run SEO in parallel, explain their crawl and schema approach, and never promise a fixed spot inside ChatGPT.
key_takeaways: Start every conversation by asking for a live look at what AI engines say about you.
A real plan names specific pages, technical fixes and questions, not just tactics.
Measurement should be verifiable: citations per engine, AI referral visits and leads.
Promises of guaranteed placement in AI answers are a red flag.
Compare proposals on the same scorecard so price is not the only thing you see.

sections.heading: Why choosing a GEO agency is harder than choosing an SEO agency
sections.body_html:
Generative engine optimization is young. Many agencies have added "AI" to an existing SEO menu without changing how they work, and the results of GEO are harder to see than a ranking report. That makes it easy to buy the wrong thing.

The good news is that you can test most of what matters before you sign anything. A capable agency can show you, in a single call, how ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews currently answer your buyers' questions, and explain why you are or are not in those answers.

sections.heading: The 10-point checklist to choose a GEO agency
sections.body_html:
1. They show your baseline first. Before pitching, they run real buyer questions through several AI engines and show who gets cited.
  2. They name specific pages. Their plan says which of your pages they would rebuild and which new pages they would create, and why.
  3. They explain crawl access. They can tell you which AI crawlers, such as OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended, your robots.txt allows today, and what they recommend.
  4. They treat structure seriously. Schema, a clean sitemap, internal links and an llms.txt file are part of the plan, not an afterthought.
  5. They write for passages. They talk about direct answers, question headings, comparison tables and sourced facts, because that is what AI engines quote.
  6. They build authority off your site. They have a plan for consistent brand descriptions and earned mentions, not just on-page edits.
  7. They keep SEO healthy. They protect existing rankings, because many AI answers draw on pages that already rank.
  8. They measure what you care about. Citations per engine, AI referral sessions and leads by page, each one something you can verify.
  9. They are honest about time. They expect early wins on specific questions within months and slower progress on broad ones.
  10. They make no placement promises. Nobody controls AI answers. An agency that says otherwise is selling certainty it does not have.

sections.heading: Red flags that should end the conversation
sections.body_html:
• Promised positions: "We'll get you to #1 in ChatGPT" is not something anyone can deliver.
  • Volume over quality: plans to publish hundreds of thin, near-identical pages. Google's spam policies specifically target scaled content that adds little value, and AI engines rarely quote it.
  • Secret methods: if they cannot explain what they will change on your site, you cannot judge it.
  • No baseline: without a before-and-after test of the same questions, improvement is impossible to prove.
  • Blocking AI crawlers by default: some security setups block the very bots that power AI search. An agency should check this in week one.

sections.heading: How to compare GEO proposals side by side
sections.body_html:
Put every proposal on the same scorecard so the comparison is fair:

QuestionWhat a strong answer looks like
What does AI say about us now?Screenshots or a table of answers for your real buyer questions
What changes first?A named list of pages, fixes and new topics, with reasons
How is progress measured?Citations per engine, AI referral visits, leads by page, Search Console data
What does month one deliver?Audit, crawl and schema fixes, tracking set up
Who does the work?Named people, with how often you meet them
What do you need from us?A clear, small list: access, approvals, subject-matter input

Price matters, but compare it only after you know what each agency will actually do.

sections.heading: Questions to ask on the first call
sections.body_html:
• Which three questions would you most want us to be cited for, and why?
  • What would you change on our homepage and our best service page?
  • How do you decide which AI engines to prioritize for our buyers?
  • Can you show a past report, with client details removed?
  • How do you handle content approvals and our brand voice?
  • What happens if a change hurts our existing rankings?

Listen for specifics about your site. Generic answers usually mean a generic service.

sections.heading: What a good GEO agency will ask you
sections.body_html:
Choosing well works both ways. The agencies worth hiring will want to understand your business before they promise anything, so expect questions like these on the first call:

  • Who are your best customers, and what do they ask before they buy? The questions buyers ask AI assistants are the raw material of a GEO plan.
  • Which competitors do you lose to, and where do they show up that you do not? Competitors already cited by AI engines show what the engines currently trust.
  • What proof do you have? Case studies, reviews, certifications and real numbers are what make a page worth quoting.
  • Who can approve changes, and how fast? GEO depends on editing real pages, so slow approvals slow results.
  • How do leads reach you today? If the site has no clear next step, extra visibility will not turn into revenue.

If an agency skips these and goes straight to a price, it is probably selling a package rather than a plan built for you. The best proposals read like they could only have been written for your business.

sections.heading: Local versus remote GEO agencies
sections.body_html: GEO is mostly remote work, so you can hire anywhere. A local agency still helps when your buyers search locally, for example "best accountant in Orange County", because it will understand the local competitors, directories and review sites that AI engines lean on for those answers. For national or online businesses, choose on expertise and measurement rather than location.

faqs.q: How do I choose a GEO agency?
faqs.a: Ask each agency to show what AI engines say about your brand today, name the specific pages and fixes they would start with, and explain how they measure citations, AI-referred visits and leads. Compare proposals on the same scorecard and avoid anyone promising fixed placement.

faqs.q: What is a red flag when hiring a GEO agency?
faqs.a: Promises of guaranteed positions in ChatGPT or other engines, plans to mass-produce thin pages, and methods they will not explain. Each of these suggests the agency is selling certainty rather than real improvements you can verify.

faqs.q: Should a GEO agency also do SEO?
faqs.a: Yes. Many AI answers draw on pages that already rank in search, so keeping technical SEO, content quality and links healthy supports GEO. An agency that ignores SEO can undo existing results.

faqs.q: How much proof should I expect before signing?
faqs.a: At minimum, a live baseline of how AI engines answer your buyers' questions, a page-level plan, and an example report. A capable agency can produce the baseline quickly because it is the first thing they would do anyway.

faqs.q: Is a local GEO agency better?
faqs.a: Only if your buyers search locally. Local knowledge helps with regional competitors, directories and reviews that feed local AI answers. Otherwise, choose on expertise, transparency and measurement.

faqs.q: How long should a first GEO contract be?
faqs.a: Three months is a sensible first term: long enough to audit, fix, publish and re-test, and short enough to judge whether the agency is delivering before you commit further.
